terminal.description: A terminal in your workspace. `node ask.js server.js` starts your server, sends it each request in `requests.txt`, shows every answer and what the server printed, then stops it.

tasks.title: Answer each address in its own way
tasks.description:
`server.js` is the server from the last issue: for now every request gets the free plots. Change it so that the address decides the answer. All three are plain text with status 200:

- `GET /` answers `Marrowfield Allotment Society. Try /plots or /free.`
- `GET /plots` answers every plot of `plots.txt`, one a line, with its holder or `free`:

```
A1: Maud Pask
A2: Lionel Barnes
A3: free
```

- `GET /free` answers the free plots, as before.

Check starts your server with a `plots.txt` of its own and sends a request to each address.
nextSteps: Run `node ask.js server.js` and look at what each request in `requests.txt` gets now.
In the function that answers, look at the path of the request, `req.url`.
Give each of the three paths its own answer, with an `if` for each.
For `/plots`, write one line for each plot, with `free` where the holder is empty.
hints: The function given to `createServer` runs for every request, whatever its address. It is your code that tells the addresses apart.
`req.url` is the address without the computer's name: `/plots` for `http://localhost:3000/plots`. Compare it, and `return` after each answer so only one is sent.

tasks.title: Say when an address or a method is wrong
tasks.description:
Change `server.js` so that a wrong request gets a status that says what is wrong, still as plain text:

- An address that is not one of the three, such as `GET /gate` or `GET /plots/A1`, gets status `404` and the body `No page at /gate.`, with the path asked for. That holds whatever the method.
- One of the three addresses with a method other than `GET`, such as `POST /plots`, gets status `405`, the header `Allow: GET`, and the body `Only GET works at /plots.`

Check sends requests to addresses that are not there and to the three with other methods, then a `GET /plots`.
nextSteps: Add `GET /gate` and `DELETE /free` to `requests.txt`, and see what they get now.
First decide whether the path is one of the three; if not, answer 404.
Then look at `req.method`; if it is not `GET`, answer 405 with the `Allow` header.
Only then answer the three addresses as in task 1.
hints: A status of 200 tells every program that all went well. A page that is not there, answered with 200, looks like a page whose text is "No page".
`req.method` is the method in capitals, such as `'GET'` or `'POST'`. 404 means the address is not there at all; 405 means it is there, but not for this method.
``if (req.method !== 'GET') { res.statusCode = 405; res.setHeader('Allow', 'GET'); res.end(`Only GET works at ${path}.`); return }``.

tasks.title: Read the row from the query
tasks.description:
People by the tap want only the free plots of their row. Change `server.js` so that `GET /free?row=B` answers:

```
Free plots in row B: B2.
```

or `No free plots in row D.` when that row has none. The row is a plot's letter, typed in either case: `row=b` is row B too. With no `row`, or an empty one, `/free` answers every free plot as before.

A query never changes which address it is: `/plots?sort=holder` is still `/plots`, and `/?from=noticeboard` is still `/`. Read the query with the URL tools built into Node, so that a query with several names, in any order, works too.

Check sends requests with queries of its own, with other names around `row` and with the row written in code, the way addresses write some letters.
nextSteps: Add `GET /free?row=B` to `requests.txt` and run `node ask.js server.js`: what path does your code see now?
Make a `URL` from `req.url`, and use its `pathname` wherever you compared the path.
Read `row` from its `searchParams`, and keep only the free plots that start with that letter.
Say so when the row has none.
hints: `req.url` holds the query too: `/free?row=B`. Compared as it is, it matches none of your paths.
`new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')` needs a full address, so give it any computer's name as the second part. Its `pathname` is the path alone, and `searchParams.get('row')` the row, or `null`.
